subject: English
passage:
The following text is adapted from Willa Cather's 1918 novel My Ántonia. Jim is a young man living in rural Nebraska who has formed a close friendship with his neighbor Ántonia.

Ántonia alone understood [Jim]. The rest of the townspeople were of little consequence to him. Fellow students might compliment or seek his company; but he remained detached beneath their attention, and from an overly familiar classmate he would simply turn and leave. When Ántonia's brothers, Ambrosch and Marek, came to town for the harvest festival, Jim paid them no mind until he realized they were dear to Ántonia; only then did he acknowledge them in a grudging manner, accepting their invitations as though he were doing them a kindness by participating.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Jim has become more withdrawn since he began his friendship with Ántonia.
choices.B: Jim distrusts his peers and does his best to keep away from them.
choices.C: Jim values Ántonia more highly than he does any other person.
choices.D: Jim has been particularly popular among most of Ántonia's family members.

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most accurately states the main idea of the text. After establishing that Jim views other townspeople as having "little consequence," the text explains that Jim won't acknowledge people other than Ántonia unless they matter to Ántonia, and even then he's only grudgingly accepting. Thus, the text focuses on the idea that Ántonia has a special importance in Jim's mind, with Jim valuing her more highly than other people.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect because the text conveys that Jim doesn't really connect with people other than Ántonia and is detached toward them. However, there's no indication that Jim distrusts and avoids people generally; indeed, he values Ántonia, who is also a person.
